title: Context Compression Policy
description: Defines when context compression renders evidence untrusted, tracking of compression levels, session rotation triggers, and the prohibition on using compressed summaries as primary evidence.

compressionDefinition.description: Context compression is any operation that reduces the active context window of an agent session by summarizing, truncating, or eliding prior conversation or evidence. This includes both automatic (system-triggered) and manual (user-triggered) compression.

types.description: Automatic context compression triggered by the runtime when token budget is exceeded.
types.detection: Check for context-compression events in AGENT_PROGRESS.jsonl or transcript markers.

types.description: User or agent requested summarization of prior context.
types.detection: Check for /summarize or equivalent commands in transcript.

types.description: Prior session content truncated when starting a new session.
types.detection: Check for discontinuity in transcript timestamps or agent session IDs.

compressionLevelTracking.description: Each agent session must track how many compressions have occurred.

0.label: No Compression
0.description: No compression events detected. All evidence from this session is fully trusted.

1.label: Single Compression
1.description: One compression event. Evidence created after compression is trusted; evidence summarized during compression is untrusted.
1.rule: Evidence entries whose timestamp precedes the first compression event are flagged as potentially summarized.

2.label: Double Compression
2.description: Two compression events. All pre-compression evidence is untrusted. Session should prepare for rotation.
2.rule: Only evidence created after the second compression event retains trust. Session rotation recommended.

3.label: Triple Compression
3.description: Three or more compression events. All evidence from this session is untrusted. Session rotation is mandatory.
3.rule: Entire session evidence is distrusted. Worker must be re-spawned with fresh context.

sessionRotationTrigger.description: After 2-3 compressions, the session must rotate: the worker's context is considered exhausted and a fresh session must be spawned.

triggers.description: Immediately stop work. Generate handoff. Re-spawn worker with fresh context.
Worker should complete current atomic unit of work, then generate handoff and rotate.
No rotation required but compression level must be recorded in progress events.

sessionRotationTrigger.handoffRequirement: Every rotation must produce a handoff JSON artifact with SHA256 hash of current state, per session-rotation protocol.

summaryAsEvidenceProhibition.description: Summaries produced during or after context compression are explicitly prohibited as primary evidence.

rules.description: Any evidence entry whose content was summarized during compression cannot be used as primary evidence for a PASS verdict.
A summary cannot override or contradict a verifier result.
If a summary must be referenced, it must be corroborated by at least one tier 1-4 evidence item that was created after the last compression event.
Any evidence entry created in a session with compression > 0 must declare its compressionLevel in metadata.

crossSessionEvidence.description: Evidence spanning multiple sessions due to rotation.
rules: Each session's evidence is independently evaluated for compression trust.
Evidence from a session with compression level 3 is excluded from all verdicts.
Handoff artifacts must carry the compression level of the session they close.
The replacement session starts at compression level 0.
